title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
abstract: arXiv:2611.05802v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent LLM-centric advances can generate attractive furnished rooms by selecting and arranging assets. Yet evaluation remains limited to specific perspectives or predefined questions, failing to reflect overall scene quality. To address this pressing need, we introduce GREP. Its core is a focus shift from defining specific questions to establishing a three-tier evaluation philosophy: basic physical validity checks whether a scene obeys physical constraints; visual coherence concerns compatibility in object scale, style, and composition; and, at the highest level, human-use logic requires object arrangements to align with everyday human habits. Guided by these principles, an evaluation agent autonomously and adaptively identifies issues from scene context, gathers evidence, and produces scores and reports. translated_title: GREP：基于原则的生成式房间评估
translated_abstract: 近期以大语言模型（LLM）为核心的进展能够通过选择和布置物体资产来生成美观的带家具房间。然而，现有评估仍局限于特定视角或预定义的问题，无法反映场景的整体质量。为满足这一迫切需求，我们提出了 GREP。其核心是将关注点从定义具体问题转变为建立一套三层评估理念：基础物理有效性检查场景是否遵守物理约束；视觉连贯性关注物体在尺度、风格和构图上的兼容性；而在最高层级，人类使用逻辑要求物体的布置符合人类的日常习惯。在这些原则的指导下，一个评估智能体能够自主且自适应地从场景上下文中识别问题、收集证据，并生成评分和报告，从而支持针对具体场景的问题发现和可靠判断。实验表明：(1) GREP 与人类评估达成 87% 的一致性……
tldr: GREP 提出了包含物理有效性、视觉连贯性和人类使用逻辑的三层评估理念，通过自主评估智能体发现场景问题并生成评分与报告，使生成房间的评估与人类判断达到 87% 的一致性。
en_tdlr: GREP grounds generated room evaluation in a three-tier philosophy—physical validity, visual coherence, and human-use logic—using an autonomous evaluation agent to identify scene-specific issues and produce scores and reports, achieving 87% agreement with human judgments.
